evidence.quote: From {{inh|en|enm|schrewed|t=depraved; wicked|lit=accursed}}, from {{m|enm|schrewen|t=to curse; beshrew}}, from {{m|enm|schrewe}}, {{m|enm|schrowe}}, {{m|enm|screwe|t=evil or wicked person/thing}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċrēawa|t=wicked person|lit=biter}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|shrew|ed}}. More at [[shrew]]. The sense of "cunning" developed in early 16<sup>th</sup> c., gradually gaining a positive connotation by 17<sup>th</sup> c.
"wicked, depraved, malicious, evil," from shrewe "wicked man" (see shrew) + -ed. Compare… See origin and meaning of shrewd. from shrewe "wicked man" (see shrew ) + -ed .
